title: Direct Spatiotemporal Imaging of Charge Carrier Dynamics in Operative Semiconductor Devices
authors: Adriano Cola, Antonio Valletta, Isabella Farella, Vaclav Dědič, Lorenzo Dominici
abstract: Understanding charge carrier dynamics within electronic devices is crucial, as it governs both the internal evolution of signals and the externally measurable current. Yet, direct imaging of these dynamics remains elusive: existing approaches are often indirect or inherently perturbative. Here, we introduce Carrier Dynamics by Pockels Imaging (CDPI), a sensitive, quantitative, and non-invasive method that enables direct access to internal charge dynamics. By probing the local electric field, CDPI visualizes photogenerated electron clouds in real space while simultaneously correlating their evolution with both conduction and displacement currents, thereby establishing a unified picture of carrier transport. The technique provides direct insight into fundamental mechanisms \textemdash including drift, diffusion, carrier-carrier interactions, trapping and detrapping \textemdash as well as the spatiotemporal evolution of carrier cloud morphology. Demonstrated in CdTe radiation detectors with micrometre-scale spatial resolution and nanosecond temporal resolution, CDPI is broadly applicable to systems exhibiting appreciable electro-optic responses. Beyond conventional semiconductors, the approach extends to organic, perovskite, and two-dimensional optoelectronic materials, offering a new paradigm for directly linking internal carrier dynamics to device-level functionality.
summary: The paper introduces Carrier Dynamics by Pockels Imaging (CDPI), a novel, non-invasive method that uses the electro-optic effect to directly image how photogenerated charge carriers move inside semiconductor devices. By correlating these internal field measurements with external current readings, researchers can map fundamental transport processes like drift and diffusion in real time. This technique offers a powerful new tool for understanding device physics across diverse optoelectronic materials.
main_problem: Directly imaging charge carrier dynamics within active semiconductor devices is challenging because existing measurement techniques are often indirect or perturbative.
main_result: The proposed technique, CDPI, successfully visualizes internal electron cloud evolution in real space while simultaneously correlating it with measurable conduction and displacement currents. This establishes a unified picture of carrier transport mechanisms like drift and diffusion.
method: The method uses Carrier Dynamics by Pockels Imaging (CDPI), which non-invasively probes the local electric field via the electro-optic effect to map photogenerated electron clouds.
model_or_system: The study is demonstrated in CdTe radiation detectors and is applicable to various optoelectronic materials like perovskites. The analysis models charge transport by relating the measured electric field variations to fundamental current components (conduction and displacement).
key_observables: Electric field distribution $E(y, t)$, electron cloud density $\delta n$, conduction current ($I_{cond}$), and displacement current.
important_parameters: Micrometre-scale spatial resolution and nanosecond temporal resolution; voltage biases ranging from 50 V to 200 V; varying optical irradiation power densities.
main_assumptions: The derivation of the total current often assumes negligible diffusion when relating it solely to electric field derivatives. The analysis relies on detailed device simulation parameters for material properties like trap levels and mobilities.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setup using pump-probe beams, time-space charts showing electric field differences, and profiles comparing internal charge cloud evolution with external measured currents (conduction/displacement).
paper_structure: The paper introduces CDPI as a solution to direct imaging limitations. It details the physical principles linking EO measurements to current components, presents experimental demonstrations in CdTe, and discusses applicability across various semiconductor types.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state electronics, the core concept of using an external optical probe (Pockels effect) to map internal field dynamics—a non-invasive measurement technique—is highly relevant for studying open quantum systems or charge transfer in nanoscale devices where direct probing is difficult.
